general_proof_review.finite_product: Distribute (f_s+df)(g_s+dg), subtract f_s*g_s, and retain f_s*dg+g_s*df+df*dg. Equivalently f_s*dg+df*g_t. No limiting assumption removes the interaction.
general_proof_review.block_operator: For arbitrary pair entries and real weights, distribution through (u+v)/2 proves linearity. Averaging (m,m) proves E^2=E; averaging ones proves unitality. Every block-constant output is fixed and block-constant arrays form a unital subalgebra. Constant factors c,d pull out of each finite average, proving the bimodule rule.
general_proof_review.product_identity: Set qf=f-Ef and qg=g-Eg. Linearity/idempotence imply E(qf)=E(qg)=0. Expand fg=Ef*Eg+Ef*qg+qf*Eg+qf*qg. Range closure fixes Ef*Eg under E; the factor rule kills the two mixed coarse terms. Hence E(fg)=Ef*Eg+E(qf*qg) and Q(fg)=Ef*qg+qf*Eg+Q(qf*qg). The mixed terms remain in Q, and the coarse part of qf*qg remains in E(fg).
general_proof_review.finite_basis_checks: The verifier checks E^2=E on all four basis vectors; the full bilinear product identity on all 16 ordered pairs of input basis vectors; and the trilinear bimodule identity on all 2x4x2 combinations of coarse/input/coarse basis vectors. Together with the explicit linearity and pointwise-bilinearity formulas, these exhaust the stated finite-array identities rather than relying only on sampled data.
general_proof_review.counterexample: E_star(x,y,z)=(x,x,z+y-x) is linear, unital, idempotent and has multiplicatively closed range (a,a,b). Missing bimodule property yields factor sides (0,0,1) versus (0,0,0), and proposed Q RHS minus direct equals (0,0,-2). This is an intentionally preserved counterexample, not a failed course computation.
general_proof_review.singular: K(u,v)=(u+v,2(u+v)); necessity of j2=2*j1 follows directly. When compatible, setting v=t and u=j1-t proves sufficiency and parametrizes every solution. When incompatible, rho=(0,j2-2*j1) preserves the obstruction relative to the declared first-equation-matching view. The finite parameter checks illustrate this symbolic argument, not prove the real-parameter claim by sampling.
general_proof_review.ledger: Pair means and signed details invert by (m-d,m+d). Anchored cumulative addition reverses differences. Composition reverses in order 3,2,1 and retains all four signed reconstruction errors, including zeros.

independent_recomputation.auditor_only_extension: A three-entry single mean block with f=(0,1,2), g=(0,1,4) gives Q(qf*qg)=(1/3,-4/3,1), not zero, and Q(fg)=(-3,-2,5). This checks that the general formula retains the term even though its Q part vanishes in every taught equal-pair example. It is not an additional course requirement or student assessment.
